title: Truth teaches (Imitation 1.3)
hook: happy is the one whom truth teaches directly
tomorrow: where's a kingdom you can't point to on a map?

segments.voice: Yesterday the Imitation's first chapter put the sorrow ahead of the definition. Yesterday's line: doing over defining.

A screenshot goes around the group chat, and three friends offer three readings of one short reply. Everyone's an interpreter; nobody asks the person who sent it. The third chapter of the Imitation has a strange detail for that moment. It's a book, made entirely of words, and it says the best teacher isn't words at all. Happy, it says, is the one whom truth teaches directly. So who's doing the teaching, once the books run out?
screen: `THREE FRIENDS, THREE READINGS.` → `A BOOK AGAINST WORDS?` → `TRUTH TEACHES DIRECTLY.`

segments.voice: The chapter's opening, in its sense: happy is the one whom truth teaches by itself, not through figures and words that pass away, but as it really is. Our own opinions and senses, it says, often fool us, and see very little. Then the puzzle's answer: the teacher is a someone. The one to whom the eternal Word speaks is set free from a crowd of opinions. From that one Word all things come, and all things speak of him. That's the language of John's Gospel: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." So a book can say this without tripping over itself. It's pointing past its own pages, like a friend who says: don't take my word for it, go and meet him. And it's careful not to sneer at study. Learning isn't to be blamed, it says; knowledge is good in itself. But a good conscience and a good life come first, and a humble knowledge of yourself is a surer road to God than deep searching after learning. Then a glance at the famous teachers of its day: where are they now? Others hold their places and hardly think of them.
screen: `OPINIONS SEE VERY LITTLE.` · `THE ETERNAL WORD SPEAKS.` · `A BOOK POINTING PAST ITSELF.` · `KNOW YOURSELF, HUMBLY.` · then, large: `TRUTH TEACHES.`

segments.voice: Set the words down for the sit. Choose one sound around you, a fan, traffic, a bird, your own breath, and let it be exactly what it is, without naming or explaining it. If you pray, you can simply listen.
Truth teaches. The Imitation's hope that truth itself, the eternal Word, teaches a person directly, as it is.
Keep this one: truth teaches, and even this book's pages point past themselves. See you tomorrow.
